html:
A column of purple porphyry stone set up in the centre of the oval Forum of Constantine in Constantinople, to mark the city's dedication on 11 May 330. It is the oldest monument of Constantine's city still standing in Istanbul.

It stood on the Mese, the main street. A statue of Constantine, shown as the sun god Apollo, stood on top until a storm threw it down in 1106. Legends grew around the base: it was said to hold holy relics, and even the Palladium brought from Rome.

Fires, earthquakes and time damaged the shaft. Around 1515 the Ottomans bound it with iron hoops, which gave it its Turkish name, Çemberlitaş, the "hooped stone". In English it is often called the Burnt Column, after the blackening from fires. It belongs to the same moment as the founding of the city and the enlarged Hippodrome.
